title: The organ man pulling his hurdy-gurdy through the streets
summary: Williams describes the street organ man who played three tunes for a nickel and drank beer, with kids running behind.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Where was Nick of Themis from here, my band?
From around there, D.A. Liberty. What did he play? No, he didn't play nothing, not as I know of.
I thought he played that, uh...

Organ? Organ. Oh, the, the, the, what the, hoody good? Yeah. Well, well, I mean, he done that for money. Oh, yeah. You see, they played, they pulled them around the street and got percentage. You see? Mm-hmm. Yeah, he used to pull the hoody good and the organ around. We call it, now y'all come the organ man, you know, see. Well, he was working, he wasn't playing nothing, you know, see. Yeah, there wasn't...
No. There wasn't any special thing without you just turning the knob on there? Just turning the knob, yeah.

Did that have a special rhythm? No, like a piano, you know. I guess, I swear it must have had in it I guess. But you turn it with your hand, you see. And they just go from corner to corner, catch the spots like that, this corner's the saloon. They play three pieces for nickels, see. You'd give them a nickel and they'd play your three numbers. Well, all right, he'd go to the next corner, they'd have anybody going to music. Now he'd play one number just to draw the people, you understand, see. Then the guy come out of the bar and he'd have drunk, say, come on man, play my nickels worth of music. Well, he'd play three numbers. Then he'd go in there, he always had his beer bucket hanging on it, all his auger. And he'd go in there and get drunk. Well, he'd play for nothing. After he'd get drunk, just keep on turning, come out there and play a tune and go in there and get him some beer and come back and play again. Sometime he'd stay there two or three hours. Sometime he'd get so drunk he couldn't pull the auger. Of course, he had to pull it, he didn't have no horse pull it, he was the horse. Boy, it was kicks, I'm telling you. It really was kicks, the auger man. And little kids would just run behind him, you know how little children are. I was in the gang running behind him too. I was small, about eight, nine years old.
He was older than Nicodemus. Oh, yeah, oh, yeah.
He was a man when we were kids.
